A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HComP-Net and contain readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. The original material can be matched across formatting changes, relocations, and figure renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, unseen-species generalization, prototype-purity, ablation, and qualitative results on birds, butterflies, and fishes, including supplementary experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds spider and turtle evaluations, additional classification baselines, and qualitative analyses.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.4 retain the architecture, prototype assignment, losses, masking mechanism, and training procedure. The expanded abstract describes components already present in v1; new benchmark configurations do not introduce a new method.

E1.justification: v2 adds iNat2021 evaluations covering 113 spider species and 41 turtle species alongside the original three datasets. These introduce additional organism groups and naturalistic images with clutter, occlusion, and blur, substantially broadening evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds ConvNeXt-tiny, ProtoPNet, and PIP-Net to the original ResNet-50, INTR, and HPnet comparison. These additions are evaluated on the original three datasets as well as the new datasets, substantially strengthening comparator coverage. The unseen-species and hierarchical-purity comparator remains HPnet.

E3.justification: Protocols for the original datasets remain unchanged. The new evaluations introduce GroundingDINO cropping and filtering at 50% confidence and HPnet tuning of prototype length, learning rate, and push frequency. Section 4 specifies 20 prototypes for 'Spider and Lizard,' conflicting with Appendix C's retained statement of 10 for all experiments; the intended Turtle budget is unclear.

E4.justification: New Figure 7 presents misclassified spider and turtle images to examine difficult backgrounds, blur, and occlusion; Figure 13 adds prototype case studies for these groups. Existing loss, prototype-count, thresholding, and high-resolution HPnet analyses are retained, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Appendix E retains five random initializations and the same 70.63% mean accuracy with 0.18% standard deviation, merely making the Bird attribution explicit. Existing part-purity uncertainty reporting is unchanged; the added classification results introduce no new uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Table 1 substantially expands the reported results: HComP-Net achieves 76.19% on Spider and 58.26% on Turtle, while newly included PIP-Net exceeds its accuracy on all five datasets. Original classification entries, unseen-species results, and ablation values remain unchanged. The changed comparative picture comes from added results, not improved same-setting HComP-Net scores.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and reasoning in Equations 1–9, including the losses, masking score, and post-hoc thresholding formulation, are unchanged. Neither version adds formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claims concerning common, discriminative hierarchical prototypes, masking, semantic consistency, unseen-species generalization, and evolutionary-hypothesis generation are retained. The abstract foregrounds previously stated contributions, while the additional datasets extend supporting evidence without redefining the core contribution.

C2.justification: v2 replaces the accuracy-focused interpretation in Section 5.1 with emphasis on discovering meaningful traits and discusses difficulties from noisy images. Section 4 explicitly excludes global-contour traits. Appendix M expands the discussion of subjective interpretation, viewing angles, multiple-image visualization, and a possible ProtoConcepts extension.

D1.justification: Appendix F adds HPnet tuning details, spider/turtle filtering instructions, and dataset and phylogeny statistics. References add direct data-source links. The repository is already disclosed in v1; the new reproducibility statements largely repeat existing access information, and some new benchmark settings remain inconsistently documented.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds positioning against hierarchical classification, taxonomy regularization, and concept-whitening approaches, emphasizing localized fine-grained attributes. v2 also explicitly credits HPnet's earlier hierarchical-prototype contribution and discusses ProtoConcepts in the limitations. The principal relationship to prototype-based work remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 expands the abstract, related work, experimental discussion, and limitations, and adds reproducibility statements. It updates authorship, publication headers, and citation style. Most prose, section ordering, and the appendix organization remain recognizable, so this is a limited revision rather than a wholesale rewrite.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains comparator rows and dataset columns; Tables 7–8 gain dataset rows. Two figures are added for misclassifications and spider/turtle prototypes. Existing figures are retained and renumbered, while the conference template changes headers, typography, and table placement without substantially redesigning the visual material.

improvement.justification: v2 provides a more informative empirical comparison by including the backbone and closely related prototype baselines, extending evaluation to naturalistic spider/turtle images, and explaining accuracy and applicability limitations more clearly. These gains improve transparency without requiring higher HComP-Net scores. Their overall extent is limited: the new semantic evidence is qualitative, and conflicting prototype-count statements weaken reproducibility of the added evaluations.
